description:
Programme Overview

The International Max Planck Research School for Chemistry and Physics of Quantum Materials (IMPRS-CPQM) has opened its 2027 call with more than twenty doctoral projects on offer. The school is a tri-institutional collaboration: the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids in Dresden, Technische Universitaet Dresden, and the University of St Andrews in Scotland. Each project pairs a specific supervisor with a defined research question across condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry.

The subject matter spans the chemistry-physics boundary of quantum materials - how new compounds are grown and characterised, and how their electronic, magnetic and topological behaviour is measured and modelled. Because every project is advertised individually with its own page, applicants should read the project list on the school website and target the two or three projects closest to their background.

What Is on Offer

The 2027 call at a glance
ComponentDetails
ProjectsMore than 20 doctoral projects in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry.
InstitutionsMax Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids (Dresden), TU Dresden, University of St Andrews.
FundingFully funded doctoral employment contracts under Max Planck Society / TU Dresden scales; health insurance, pension and social benefits included.
DeadlineApplications accepted no later than 30 November 2026.
EligibilityHighly motivated candidates with an outstanding bachelor's or master's degree well aligned with the school's research areas.

Who Should Apply

Candidates finishing a bachelor's or master's degree in physics, chemistry, materials science or a neighbouring field whose interests sit in quantum materials - superconductivity, magnetism, topology, correlated electron systems, crystal growth or the solid-state chemistry behind them. The school explicitly welcomes applications from candidates whose degree is 'well-aligned' rather than identical to the project topics, so a strong methods background matters more than an exact subject match.

How to Apply

Applications run through the school's own application system, following the detailed application guidelines published on the IMPRS-CPQM website. The usual package - CV, transcripts, two referees and a statement of research interests tied to specific advertised projects - should be prepared before starting the form, and each project page on the school site tells you which supervisor to reference.

Why Dresden

Dresden is one of Europe's densest clusters for materials research: the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids, TU Dresden's ct.qmat cluster and a wider campus of Leibniz institutes sit within walking distance of each other. Doctoral researchers in Max Planck schools are employed with full contracts, and Dresden's living costs remain well below those of Munich, Stuttgart or Frankfurt, which stretches a German doctoral salary a long way.
